rules_text:
Rules summary Template:Infobox game Custodian Dice is an abstract strategy game played on a 5 × 5 grid. Players capture opposing dice by surrounding them on multiple sides. Contents 1 Objective 2 Components 3 Setup 4 Gameplay 4.1 Select 4.2 Move or Jump 4.2.1 Jumping 4.3 Rotate or Flip 4.3.1 If the die moved 4.3.2 If the die jumped 4.4 Capture 5 End of the Game 6 Variants 6.1 No Jumping Variant 6.2 Chaos Reigns Supreme Objective Capture enough of your opponent’s pieces so they are no longer able to capture any of yours. Components 1 5 × 5 game board 10 regular dice 5 dice in one colour 5 dice in another colour Setup Each player takes five dice of their own colour and rolls them. Each player places their five dice in a starting line on the row of the board closest to them. Gameplay A player’s turn consists of four steps: Select Move or Jump Rotate or Flip Capture Select Choose one of your available dice. Move or Jump Move the selected die exactly as many spaces as shown on its top face. When moving, you may not: Move diagonally Move over other pieces Move back onto a space you just left You may change direction during movement, as long as the full movement total is completed and all movement is orthogonal. Jumping Instead of moving normally, if your die is adjacent to any other die and there is an empty space directly behind that die, you may jump over it. You cannot both move and jump on the same turn. You must choose one or the other. Rotate or Flip After moving or jumping, the selected die must change faces. If the die moved Rotate the selected die 90° to one of its adjacent faces. The die may not be rotated to its opposite face. For example, if the die shows 1, it may be rotated to 2, 3, 4, or 5, but not 6. If the die jumped Flip the selected die to its opposite face. Opposite faces are: 1 ↔ 6 2 ↔ 5 3 ↔ 4 Capture After movement and rotation or flipping, check for captures. Pieces are captured by Custodial Capture . To capture an opposing die, it must be sandwiched between two of your dice in a straight orthogonal line. A piece is only captured when the active player creates the sandwiching position. Moving your own die into a position where it is sandwiched does not cause it to be captured. Multiple simultaneous captures are possible from a single move, including multi-layered sandwich captures. End of the Game The game ends as soon as one player has fewer than two dice remaining. That player loses. Variants No Jumping Variant For a more restrictive game, remove jumping from the available movement options. This makes movement more cramped and makes it harder to escape certain positions, while also reducing the mental overhead of considering jump moves. Chaos Reigns Supreme Instead of rotating or flipping a die after moving or jumping, roll the die. Whichever face it lands on becomes its new face until it moves again.

---

[Rating: 1/10] I assumed it would be like Devil Dice. It's not, the dice rotate to almost any side you want. And it's reeeaaally slow because half the board is cluttered up with pieces in the way. And then comes the ending situation where you just run around the whole time.

[Rating: 2/10] I hate 2p combinatorial abstracts, but I enjoy dice based 2p capture games like Button Men. This is super boring. Dice can never be captured in the corners or on the edge touching another same-colored die. With both players defensively, seems like the game could never end, which I guess might a problem in some other abstracts but feels more a problem here.

[Rating: 5/10] Not bad as far as these sorts of variables movement abstract games go (Onitama, The Duke, etc). I think the customizable nature (choosing the dice fact of the die you moved) is neat. I just generally don't like two player abstracts!

[Rating: 6/10] Although simple, it was hard to get a handle on it. The play time is supposed to be 30 to 40 minutes, and it certainly took more than 20. I was pretty hapless, only making one of the four captures needed for a win. Worth trying again, I think.

[Rating: 7/10] This game is very slick except for its ending can devolve into stalemate. I don't understand the low scores here, this is one of the better dice in an abstract game I've played. I think its inclusion on BGA has got a lot of people trying it who wouldn't normally give this kind of game a go.
